experiments.question: Does an own shot-quality (xG) model add information over shot counts?
experiments.hypothesis: Distance/angle/type/strength/rebound logistic xG beats a constant goal rate out of sample.
experiments.method: Logistic regression on unblocked attempts, fitted on 2021-22 + 2022-23 only, frozen.
experiments.result: log loss validation 0.2250 vs constant 0.2547; holdout 0.2298 vs 0.2569; holdout xG sum 16915 vs 15987 goals (league finishing fell).
experiments.interpretation: xG is informative and is used as lagged player/team shot-quality features (E) and as a team-goals rating input (D); its level drifts, so it is never used as an absolute rate.

experiments.question: Which time-on-ice model should drive every skater family?
experiments.hypothesis: A role-aware model (previous game's line/PP unit from shift data) beats recency averages.
experiments.method: T_A season avg, T_B EWMA, T_C role share x team minutes, T_E LightGBM (season-blocked refits).
experiments.data: skater-games with >= 1 prior game; validation 2023-24, holdout 2024-26
experiments.result: validation total-TOI MAE A 1.980 / B 1.872 / C 1.871 / E 1.854 min; holdout E 1.821 vs B 1.844; PP-TOI MAE E 0.768 vs C 0.767.
experiments.interpretation: LightGBM on role features is best for total TOI; PP TOI is a tie between the share model and E.

experiments.question: Does the better TOI forecast improve sog (model C)?
experiments.hypothesis: Better opportunity -> better counts.
experiments.method: C with T_E minutes vs C with T_C minutes, paired CRPS on validation, game-clustered bootstrap.
experiments.interpretation: Helps shots (volume follows ice time).

experiments.question: Does the better TOI forecast improve points (model C)?
experiments.hypothesis: Better opportunity -> better counts.
experiments.method: C with T_E minutes vs C with T_C minutes, paired CRPS on validation, game-clustered bootstrap.
experiments.interpretation: No measurable effect: point production is dominated by count noise, not minutes.

experiments.question: Does the schedule-adjusted opponent factor improve sog?
experiments.hypothesis: Opponent suppression (ridge rating of shots / goals allowed) moves player outcomes.
experiments.method: D = C x factor^beta x venue; beta fitted on development (0.95, factor sog_for_oppf); validation CRPS vs A.
experiments.interpretation: The opponent/venue step helps on validation and holdout. beta ~1 for shots, >1 for scoring (the ridge goal rating is heavily pooled, so its spread understates the true opponent effect).

experiments.question: Does the schedule-adjusted opponent factor improve goals?

experiments.interpretation: The opponent/venue step helps on validation; not confirmed on holdout. beta ~1 for shots, >1 for scoring (the ridge goal rating is heavily pooled, so its spread understates the true opponent effect).

experiments.question: Why were frozen-scalar saves models biased upward?
experiments.hypothesis: Expanding-mean league priors and season-decayed ridge intercepts lag the falling league shot level.
experiments.method: Replace priors by the mean of the last 1,200 starts on earlier dates and recentre ridge shots-against on the recent team level; refit scalars on development; compare on validation.
experiments.data: validation 2023-24 (decision); holdout re-scored once afterwards and disclosed
experiments.interpretation: Verified level-drift defect; the fix is mechanical, not tuned on holdout. The holdout was therefore scored twice for saves (before/after); both are reported.

experiments.question: How much does conditioning saves on the ACTUAL starter assume?
experiments.hypothesis: Pregame starter information is nearly complete by puck drop.
experiments.method: Archived DailyFaceoff goalie observations (2026-27) vs the boxscore starter, last snapshot before start and fixed horizons.
experiments.result: last pregame snapshot correct 1.000; at T-60 / T-180 / T-360 min: 0.991 (0.62 confirmed), 0.983 (0.54 confirmed), 0.983 (0.48 confirmed)
experiments.interpretation: Conditioning on the actual starter overstates certainty by ~1-2% of starts at a 1-6 h horizon; at the final pregame snapshot it is exact in this sample. Historical seasons have no PIT source.

experiments.question: How well are tonight's lineup and PP1 known before puck drop?
experiments.hypothesis: Projected lines identify dressed skaters and PP units.
experiments.method: Last archived DailyFaceoff lines before start vs boxscore (dressed) and PP-TOI top five (PP1).
experiments.result: projected skaters who dressed 0.983; dressed skaters in the projection 0.976; PP1 precision 0.872, recall 0.876; median snapshot 44 min before start
experiments.interpretation: Lineups are ~98% knowable; PP1 is ~87% knowable. The model's PIT role uses the previous game (lines are not archived historically), so PP-unit news is an untested upside.

opponent_adjustment.summary: Opponent strength is a schedule-adjusted ridge rating (y = mu + off + def + home, refitted before every game date on all earlier games, previous seasons weighted 0.5 per season; alpha chosen on development: shots 3, goals 30, xG 3). Skater factor = (mu + opponent defence) / mu, applied as factor^beta with beta fitted on development (shots 0.95; goals/assists/points 1.20/1.30/1.26 on the goal rating, which beat the xG rating on development likelihood). Paired D - C CRPS (validation / holdout): sog -0.00197 [-0.00266, -0.00128] / -0.00175 [-0.00217, -0.00132]; goals -0.00016 [-0.00030, -0.00002] / -0.00006 [-0.00015, +0.00001]; assists -0.00035 [-0.00065, -0.00002] / -0.00021 [-0.00038, -0.00003]; points -0.00076 [-0.00135, -0.00017] / -0.00040 [-0.00072, -0.00008]. The step is clearly useful for shots, smaller for assists/points, and not confirmed on holdout for goals. A raw shrunk 'allowed' factor performs the same as the schedule-adjusted one (CIs include 0). Saves D uses ridge shots-against recentred on the recent league level (dev scale 0.938); team goals D blends ridge goals and xG ratings (goal weight 0.75).

opportunity.summary: TOI is modelled first. LightGBM on PIT role features (T_E) is the most accurate: holdout total-TOI MAE 1.821 min (EWMA 1.844, season average 1.969), PP-TOI MAE 0.768. On 2025-26 it beats PLAYER_SIM_V1's walk-forward TOI (1.842 vs 1.939) and WORKLOAD_V1's published 1.875. Role (line rank and PP unit) comes from the previous game's shift data; top-line forwards are under-projected by 0.27 min.

calibration.summary: Selected distribution: NB with mean-binned dispersion fitted on development residuals. Holdout: Shots on goal 80% cover 0.804, PIT var 0.991; Goals 80% cover 0.799, PIT var 0.997; Assists 80% cover 0.799, PIT var 0.996; Points 80% cover 0.801, PIT var 0.992; Goalie saves 80% cover 0.810, PIT var 0.985; Team goals 80% cover 0.797, PIT var 1.002. Shots need over-dispersion (Poisson PIT var ~1.03, 80% cover 0.79); goals/assists/points are Poisson (fitted alpha ~0); saves NB is slightly too wide; the game total is too wide.

summary.note: pf_core.gate run on every validation (2023-24) and holdout 2025-26 skater projection of the selected model (opportunity history = previous 10 games' TOI; stat history = previous 10 games; thresholds from the pmf; opponent sample = opponent's games this season). No projection was BLOCKed (no structural defects). REVIEW (1-3%) is driven by early-season opponent factors resting on < 3 games, role changes and thin own history; REVIEW rows have LOWER error than PASS rows because they are mostly low-volume or early-season players — the gate catches structural problems, it is not an accuracy predictor. Team reconciliation (player goal sum vs team goal model) is in section 8.

pf_core_issues: `models.group_prior_pit`: when a group has no earlier dates the default fallback is `df[col].mean()` over the whole frame — future rows included (look-ahead). Caught by our poisoned-future test; we pass a development-only fallback (`nhl.ladder.gprior`). Impact here: only rows on a group's first date (2021-22 opening night, excluded from scoring).
`pit.rolling_opponent_allowed`: same pattern — `_league` NaN is filled with the full-sample mean of `y_col`.

`models.group_prior_pit` and the ridge intercept are expanding / season-decayed means: correct point-in-time but they lag a drifting league level (NHL shots per team-game fell ~12% 2021-26). Not a bug, a property; documented fix `nhl.ladder.recent_prior`.
`lagged_features` adds columns one at a time (pandas fragmentation warnings, slow on 240k x 24 columns); harmless.
